newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to publish cellular phone tender Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Israel to publish cellular phone tender Tuesday.

text.p: The Israeli government is about to publish a tender for a third cellular telephone operator, for the first time requiring the winner to pay a licence fee, the Communications Ministry said at a news conference on Monday.

It said proposals in response to the tender, which is to be published on Tuesday, will have to be submitted by a deadline of October 28 and remain effective until August 1, 1998. Communications Minister Limor Livnat would not say when the licence would be awarded.

The third operator will compete in the Israeli cell phone market against Pelephone, a joint venture of state-owned Bezeq Israel Telecom and the Israeli subsidiary of Motorola Inc, and Cellcom, whose shareholders include Bellsouth Corp.

Doron Rosenne, the ministry's director-general, said the tender committee would use a scoring system in which the amount the bidder was prepared to pay as a licence fee would account for 75 percent, engineering and general factors for 10 percent each and benefits to the consumer for only five percent.
He said Israel's cellular market was already highly competitive so there was no reason to emphasise benefits to consumers in the scoring system.
"The situation of a third operator is different from a new operator in a monopoly market," Rosenne said.
The existing two operators share about 1.5 million subscribers, representing a penetration rate of about 26 percent.

The new license will be for two 10-megaherz frequency ranges of 900 megaherz or above. Rosenne said he assumed bidders would offer global system for mobile telecommunications (GSM)-based technology, which is used in Europe.

The Communications Ministry said a bidding consortium could be up to 80 percent foreign-controlled. Its partners must have a combined net worth of $200 million and at least 25 percent of the group must be controlled by a company already operating a cellular network outside of Israel.
The licence will be for six years with a 10-year renewal option.
In a separate announcement on Monday, Israel's Finance Ministry said the frequencies would be taken from the army which would receive $60 million a year over six years as compensation.
